body: Word worth keeping: apricity — the warmth of the sun in winter. It comes from Latin apricus, warmed by the sun, and has nothing to do with apricots, however much the tongue insists. A dictionary of 1623 recorded it and the world mostly set it down again; the workshop plans to revive it at the first sunbeam that reaches the bench.

receipts.title: Henry Cockeram — The English Dictionarie (1623), full text
quote: Apricitie. The warmenes of the Sunne in winter.

receipts.title: Wiktionary — apricity
quote: From the Latin aprīcitās, noun of quality from aprīcus ("warmed by the sun").
(obsolete) The light or warmth of the Sun.
